problems.description: Email and phone inputs have only a placeholder, no <label> or accessible name (WCAG 1.3.1 / 3.3.2 / 4.1.2). Credit if the email input (or both) is named.
Help text colour #b3b3b3 on white is about 2.1:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum (WCAG 1.4.3).
Submit is a <div onclick>: not focusable, no role, no Enter/Space handling, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot register (WCAG 2.1.1 / 4.1.2). Should be <button type="submit">.
input:focus/textarea:focus { outline: none } with no replacement focus style (WCAG 2.4.7).

Email error is shown by un-hiding a span that is not linked to the input (no aria-describedby / aria-invalid) and not in a live region, so it is not announced (WCAG 3.3.1 / 4.1.3). Credit if the output says the error is not associated with the field or not announced.
The progress image 'step 1 of 3' has no alt attribute; it conveys information (WCAG 1.1.1).
Heading levels skip from h1 to h4 (WCAG 1.3.1 best practice).

decoys.description: divider.png with alt="" is correct: it is decorative. Flagging it as missing/empty alt is a false alarm.
The terms checkbox is wrapped in its <label>, which gives it an accessible name without for/id. Flagging it as unlabelled is a false alarm.

The notes textarea has a real <label for="notes"> hidden with a standard visually-hidden class; it has an accessible name. Flagging it as unlabelled or saying the label is inaccessible is a false alarm (suggesting a visible label instead of relying on the placeholder is fine, not a false alarm).

acceptable_other_findings: No feedback is shown when the terms checkbox is unchecked (real, not planted).
Error indicated partly by red border colour (fine to mention; text also exists).
Required fields not marked with required indicator / aria-required (reasonable).
Placeholder used as instructions, autocomplete suggestions, fieldset/legend comments, page title/landmark remarks.
